title: Explicit MAD Quality Control and Robust Scaling
text: default annotation keeps original data adds one logical flag per metric plus mad_qc_outlier: [!TIP] Use transform = "none" raw-scale calculations, provide named partial overrides c(library_size = "log1p").
code: library(veryMAD)  metadata <- data.frame(   library_size = c(2e6, 31e6, 32e6, 30e6, 33e6),   mapping_rate = c(0.50, 0.92, 0.94, 0.93, 0.95),   row.names = paste0("sample", 1:5) )  annotated <- mad_qc(   metadata,   metrics = c(     library_size = "lower",     mapping_rate = "lower"   ),   transform = c(library_size = "log1p") )  annotated library_size_mad_outlier mapping_rate_mad_outlier mad_qc_outlier

title: Explicit MAD Quality Control and Robust Scaling
text: report contains three components: Thresholds retain calculation-scale raw-scale limits. Missing, undersized, zero-MAD calculations remain visible status rather silently converted decision.
code: report <- mad_qc(   metadata,   metrics = c(library_size = "lower", mapping_rate = "lower"),   transform = c(library_size = "log1p"),   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  report$thresholds report$flags report$settings names(report) #> "flags" "thresholds" "settings"

title: Explicit MAD Quality Control and Robust Scaling
text: margin = 1 scales rows; margin = 2 scales columns. Matrix dimensions dimnames preserved. Numeric data frames returned matrices.
code: values <- c(a = 1, b = 2, c = 100) mad_scale(values)  matrix_data <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 3,   dimnames = list(paste0("gene", 1:3), paste0("sample", 1:4)))  mad_scale(matrix_data, margin = 1) # scale rows mad_scale(matrix_data, margin = 2) # scale columns

title: Explicit MAD Quality Control and Robust Scaling
text: [!WARNING] MAD thresholds adaptive statistical heuristics. flag sample rejection, laboratory diagnosis, doublet call. Metrics, directions, transformations always selected explicitly. lower, upper, describe statistical tails . min_n computational safeguard, biological rule. Missing values stay missing. veryMAD filter data automatically. stratified QC, split data call mad_qc() separately.

text: sources motivate veryMAD’s explicit MAD-based QC scope also supporting guardrails: MAD flags adaptive statistical evidence, automatic biological decisions. Thresholds reviewed alongside multiple QC metrics, diagnostic plots, biological context dataset. Subramanian, ., Alperovich, M., Yang, Y., & Li, B. (2022). Biology-inspired data-driven quality control scientific discovery single-cell transcriptomics. Genome Biology, 23, 267. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-022-02820-w — Presents adaptive MAD-based QC across cell-type cluster contexts emphasizes retaining biologically meaningful populations fixed, data-agnostic thresholds can remove. Article Single-Cell Best Practices Consortium. (n.d.). Quality control. Single-cell best practices. Retrieved August 6, 2026, https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing_visualization/quality_control.html — Recommends lenient MAD-based cutoffs QC warning aggressive filtering can bias smaller subpopulations several covariates considered together. Amezquita, R. ., Lun, . T. L., Hicks, S. C., & Gottardo, R. (2021). Quality control. Basics single-cell analysis Bioconductor (Bioconductor 3.13). Bioconductor. https://bioconductor.org/books/3.13/OSCA.basic/quality-control.html#common-choices--qc-metrics — Defines common QC metrics library size, detected features, mitochondrial spike-proportions, describes adaptive MAD thresholds explicit direction transformation choices.

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
text: Rows observations metrics explicitly selects numeric QC columns. One reference distribution calculated per metric across observations; observations never filtered automatically.

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
code: mad_qc(   data,   metrics,   nmads = 3,   transform = "none",   output = c("annotate", "report"),   min_n = 5,   zero_mad = c("na", "zero", "error"),   overwrite = FALSE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
text: data data frame, tibble, numeric matrix, Seurat object. metrics non-empty named character vector mapping columns "lower", "upper", "". nmads Positive number MADs median limits. transform scalar transformation named partial overrides. Supported values "none", "log1p", "log10". output Return annotated data ("annotate") compact report ("report"). min_n Minimum number finite, non-missing observations required. zero_mad Handling zero MAD: "na", "zero", "error". overwrite Replace existing generated flag columns? verbose Print concise neutral summary?

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
text: Annotated input verymad_qc list flags, thresholds, settings.

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
code: x <- data.frame(low = c(1, 10, 11, 12, 13), high = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 20)) mad_qc(x, c(low = "lower", high = "upper"), verbose = FALSE) #>   low high low_mad_outlier high_mad_outlier mad_qc_outlier #> 1   1    1            TRUE            FALSE           TRUE #> 2  10    2           FALSE            FALSE          FALSE #> 3  11    3           FALSE            FALSE          FALSE #> 4  12    4           FALSE            FALSE          FALSE #> 5  13   20           FALSE             TRUE           TRUE

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
text: Scale numeric vector, matrix, numeric data frame median median absolute deviation. matrices, margin = 1 scales rows margin = 2 scales columns.

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
code: mad_scale(   x,   center = TRUE,   scale = TRUE,   constant = 1.4826,   na_rm = TRUE,   zero_mad = c("zero", "na", "error"),   margin = 2 )

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
text: x numeric vector, matrix, numeric data frame. center Subtract median? scale Divide MAD? constant Positive MAD consistency constant. na_rm Remove missing values calculating medians MADs? zero_mad Use zero, return NA, error zero MAD. margin Matrix margin, 1 rows 2 columns. Names "rows" "columns" also accepted.

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
text: numeric vector matrix. Matrix input preserves dimensions dimnames; data-frame input returns matrix.

title: veryMAD 0.5.1
text: Reduced exported API exactly mad_qc() mad_scale(). Removed mad_z_score() alias. Removed combine argument. mad_qc() now always returns overall mad_qc_outlier flag.

title: veryMAD 0.5.1
text: Added compact printing verymad_qc reports. Hardened empty-input, missing-value, identifier, overwrite, zero-MAD handling. Expanded tests complete public API important edge cases. Expanded continuous integration across Linux, macOS, Windows, multiple R versions.

title: veryMAD 0.5.1
text: Updated README vignettes final two-function interface. Simplified pkgdown reference index. Kept pak::pak("Thokas99/veryMAD") primary installation command.

title: veryMAD 0.5.0
text: Reduced public API mad_qc() mad_scale(). Removed grouped QC calculations separate modality workflows. Removed redundant per-result counts qualitative interpretation fields. Changed default QC transformation "none". Changed default zero-MAD policy "na".

title: veryMAD 0.5.0
text: mad_qc() provides annotation compact report outputs. QC metrics, directions, transformations remain explicit. Seurat support delegates canonical engine. mad_scale() supports robust scaling vectors matrices.

title: veryMAD 0.5.0
text: Simplified README. Added focused vignettes QC, interpretation, MAD scaling. Reorganized pkgdown website around two-function API.

title: veryMAD 0.5.0
text: Consolidated QC calculations one internal engine. Converted low-level statistical functions internal helpers. Removed duplicated wrappers obsolete implementation paths. Simplified dependencies tests.
